title: TS SDK: resumable stream demultiplexer for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Problem: Our TypeScript SDK supports both AsyncIterator and Web Streams consumers, but switching consumers mid-stream, recovering from transient network failures, and preserving backpressure semantics is brittle. Several customers reported noisy reconnections and duplicate events when attempting resumable consumption or when using consumer patterns that alternate between async iteration and ReadableStream piping.

Goal: Implement a resumable demultiplexer (demuxer) in the TS SDK that provides a stable single-stream source and allows multiple ergonomic consumption patterns: for-await-of async iteration, Web ReadableStream readers, and dual-consumer handoff. The demuxer should: preserve ordering, avoid duplicate events across resumes, propagate cancellation correctly, maintain backpressure across runtimes (Node/Deno/Browser), and provide clear APIs for developers to resume from last-acknowledged token or checkpoint.

Scope: SDK surface changes, internal framing codec to mark checkpoints, tests for Node/Deno/Browser, examples, and a short migration guide for existing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical stream source in SDK that can be consumed as AsyncIterator or ReadableStream without duplicating payloads
Ability to pause a consumer and resume later from SDK-provided checkpoint token with at-most-once semantics
Backpressure honored: if ReadableStream consumer slows, AsyncIterator-based consumer will see backpressure behavior consistent with platform capabilities
Cancellation from either consumer type cancels the underlying request and frees resources
Integration tests covering consumer swap, transient network reconnect with checkpoint resume, and stress tests showing <2% duplicate or lost messages at 1M tokens simulated workload
Documentation and two code examples (for-await-of swap-to-stream, stream-to-for-await-of) checked into docs repo
design_notes:
High-level approach: introduce a lightweight Demuxer class that owns the single wire connection and emits framed 'events' to internal sinks. Consumers can register adapters: AsyncIteratorAdapter and WebStreamAdapter. The demuxer maintains an event sequence number and persistent checkpoint token encoding the last-delivered seq number + KV cache pointer for models with KV support.

Framing: add a small opaque envelope to each chunk with metadata: seq, stableCheckpointHint, and optional resumeCursor. This is kept at the SDK layer and is backward compatible: servers ignore envelope if present.

Resumability: the demuxer can ask server for resumeCursor to seek. On transient network failure we attempt exponential-backoff reconnects and pass lastCheckpoint token to server. On resume, server unspools tokens starting after checkpoint. To avoid duplicates in edge cases we treat resume as last-delivered+1 semantics with idempotency guards in client.

Backpressure semantics: Node ReadableStream and for-await-of are different. We will implement internal pull scheduling where the demuxer only reads additional data from the network when the aggregate of registered consumers signals capacity. For dual consumers we implement a simple virtual-window counter. In runtimes that don't expose exact backpressure signals (browsers), we fall back to time-based slow-down heuristics.

Tradeoffs considered: 1) server-side complexity vs client-only: prefer client-only envelope to avoid server rollout. 2) at-least-once vs at-most-once: we aim for at-most-once with resume token, accepting small risk of message loss if server cannot replay; documented in semantics. 3) Memory vs latency: keeping unacked-message buffer reduces duplication risk on resume but increases memory; we cap buffer and use checkpoint hints to trim.
implementation_tasks: Add Demuxer core in packages/sdk/src/stream/demuxer.ts with minimal public surface
Implement AsyncIteratorAdapter and WebStreamAdapter with unified tests
Add framing encoder/decoder helpers and checkpoint token format in packages/sdk/protocol
Wire up reconnect + resume logic in runtime request loop
Add Node/Deno/Browser platform tests using playwright and node test harness
Update TypeScript SDK docs and add two examples under website/docs/streaming/resumable.md
Add telemetry events: demuxer.resume_attempt, demuxer.resume_success, demuxer.duplicate_detected
Create migration guide for existing advanced consumers
test_plan: Unit tests for framing encode/decode, sequence-number monotonicity, and token generation. Integration tests will spin up a local test server that can simulate disconnect/replay behavior and assert no duplicates across >1000 reconnect cycles. Cross-runtime tests: run browser scenario where a ReadableStream consumer pauses for 5s then resumes, and an AsyncIterator consumer resumes concurrently. Performance stress tests: measure CPU and memory overhead at 1M tokens and ensure overhead <8% compared to baseline stream path. Run CI matrix on Node 18/20, Deno latest, Chrome 120, and Firefox. Add fuzz tests to mutate checkpoint tokens.
dependencies_notes: Depends on prior streaming ergonomics work and the stream sandboxing contracts in ENG-41258 and the consumer swap policies from ENG-63012. Also coordinate with backend team to ensure resumeCursor request parameter is available in preview API if server-side replay is required.
comments: 2025-02-13 Priya Kapoor: Drafted Demuxer skeleton and basic framing. Wire protocol uses seq:uint32 and base64 resumeCursor. Started prototype in demo branch.
2025-02-18 Alex Chen: Reviewed prototype. Notes: make checkpoint token opaque (avoid leaking internal model pointers), add idempotency guard for server that may re-send last chunk on reconnection.
2025-02-21 Miguel Alvarez: Ran initial performance microbench. Demuxer adds ~3% CPU and 12KB memory per active stream at steady-state. Acceptable but add caps for long-lived idle streams.
2025-02-24 Priya Kapoor: Implemented AsyncIteratorAdapter. Found race where consumer swap + immediate cancel caused duplicate delivery; added in-flight dedupe map keyed by seq.

2025-02-27 QA: Integration harness simulated flaky network with 2s disconnects every 30s for 100 cycles. Observed 0 duplicates, 2 missing events due to server-side replay policy mismatch. Follow-up: coordinate with backend to expose resumeCursor semantics.
2025-03-03 Priya Kapoor: Addressed QA findings, added telemetry for duplicate_detected, pushed updated PR #2891 with tests. Requesting review from platform infra (Miguel) and SDK ergonomics (Sana).
Next steps: get approval from infra on resume protocol, finalize docs, and schedule rollout flag for gradual opt-in in hosted API.
